Fuel sites and tanks

Service station demolition, including the tanks underneath

Demolition of service station sites: the canopy, the shop, the forecourt and the underground fuel tanks. The tanks and the ground around them are what make this a different job from any other commercial demolition, and they are what decides the programme. Send the site details and any tank records, and we will quote the demolition and the tank removal as one job.

0456 220 552

Carried out under demolition licence AD214737

Before anything starts

Six things have to be settled first, and not all of them are ours

Most jobs that run late run late on this list rather than on the work itself. Each line says who owns it.

  1. 01

    Tank decommissioning and cleaning

    Who Specialist contractor, before we start

    Tanks emptied, cleaned, degassed and certified gas free. This is the step everything else waits on and it is not demolition work.

  2. 02

    Environmental site assessment

    Who You, through a consultant

    What is in the ground around the tanks decides the disposal classification and therefore most of the cost.

  3. 03

    Regulatory notification

    Who You and your consultant, with the relevant authority

    Removing underground petroleum storage systems is a notifiable activity with its own requirements, separate from the demolition approval.

  4. 04

    Hazardous materials survey

    Who Max, through an accredited laboratory

    The shop and canopy still need surveying for asbestos like any other commercial building.

  5. 05

    Service disconnection

    Who You, with each authority

    Power, water and any remaining gas supply.

  6. 06

    Validation plan

    Who You, through your consultant

    How the site will be shown to be clean once the tanks are out. Agreeing this before excavation starts is what stops the hole staying open.

The detail

Why the tanks decide everything

  • Nothing happens until they are gas free. Tanks have to be emptied, cleaned, degassed and certified by a specialist before any machine goes near them. That certificate is the gate.
  • The hole is bigger than the tanks. Excavation goes as far as the validation plan requires, and that extent is set by the assessment rather than by the tank dimensions.
  • The soil classification is the price. Hydrocarbon affected soil goes to a facility licensed for it. The volume and the classification together are usually the largest line on the job.
  • The hole cannot be closed until it is validated. Backfilling before the consultant has taken their samples means digging it out again.
  • Water finds the pit. An open excavation at a fuel site collects water, and that water is usually classified too.
  • The paperwork outlives the job. The validation report is what a future purchaser or certifier asks for. It is worth getting right the first time.

What has to be finished by when, and what is waiting on it

We attend the site before quoting anything substantial.

The soil, not the structure, is the number to watch

Hydrocarbon affected ground is classified before it can be priced, and the classification decides where it can go. We price the excavation and cartage on rates agreed in advance rather than a fixed figure, so the exposure is visible.

Before you book

What people ask about this one

Do you remove the underground tanks yourselves?
We excavate and remove them once a specialist contractor has emptied, cleaned, degassed and certified them gas free. That certification is not demolition work and we do not do it. What we do is coordinate the sequence so the two halves line up.
How much of the forecourt has to come out?
As far as the validation plan says, which comes from the environmental assessment rather than from us. That is why the assessment is worth doing before the quote rather than after.
Can you give a fixed price?
For the structures, yes. For the excavation and the soil disposal, not honestly, until the ground is classified. Those are priced on rates agreed before we start, so the exposure is visible rather than hidden in a contingency.
What if contamination goes beyond the site boundary?
That becomes a matter for your consultant and the relevant authority, and it is outside what a demolition contract can resolve. It is also a reason to assess before committing to a date.
How long does a service station take?
The structures are quick. The tank removal, the excavation, the validation sampling and the backfill are what make it a programme rather than a job, and the consultant’s turnaround on the samples is part of it.

Get a quote

Send the site and the assessment if you have one

The address, the number and size of the tanks, and the environmental assessment if one exists. The assessment is what turns a range into a price on this kind of site.
